candidate_relations.reason: The gastric brushings contain large non-septate, irregularly branching hyphae typical of Mucorales, not a demonstrated Basidiobolus organism.
Radiographs were unremarkable and endoscopy showed multiple mucosal nodules with invasive fungal hyphae rather than an obstructing foreign body.
Phaeohyphomycosis would show pigmented, usually septate hyphae, whereas cytology demonstrated large non-septate hyphae of irregular diameter.
Gastric phycomycosis encompasses infections historically grouped with mucormycosis and matches the pyloric site, but it does not identify the Mucorales-specific diagnosis.
Although nodular gastrointestinal disease can occur with Basidiobolus, the broad non-septate irregular hyphae in this cat support mucormycosis rather than basidiobolomycosis.
Neither imaging nor endoscopy found foreign material, while cytologic brushing directly revealed fungal hyphae within an inflamed gastric mucosa.
Aspergillus classically produces narrow septate hyphae with acute-angle branching, unlike the large non-septate irregular hyphae seen in the pyloric lesions.
The duodenum and remainder of the abdomen were normal, and the gastric nodules contained fungal hyphae rather than histologic evidence of inflammatory bowel disease.
The term phycomycosis can include mucormycosis and the disease is gastrointestinal, but it leaves the organism group and gastric predominance insufficiently specified.
Phycomycosis is an older umbrella that can contain mucormycosis, but the label omits the documented pyloric-antral disease and specific Mucorales diagnosis.
Pythiosis is an oomycete infection and is not established by the broad non-septate fungal hyphae observed in the gastric brushing.
Vomiting, gastric mucosal inflammation, and hyphae support fungal gastrointestinal disease, but this label does not identify mucormycosis or the nodular pyloric localization.
Endoscopic nodules could mimic lymphoma, but cytology showed mixed neutrophilic-macrophagic inflammation and fungal hyphae rather than neoplastic lymphocytes.
The smooth pyloric nodules are infectious lesions containing non-septate branching hyphae, with no cytologic evidence of neoplasia.
No Pythium-specific culture or histology is provided, and the observed morphology was interpreted in the setting of mucormycosis rather than pythiosis.
A raw rabbit diet is a possible exposure context, but the record does not prove foodborne transmission and this phrase does not identify the gastric Mucorales infection.
The antral location matches, but gastric pythiosis is a different organism-level diagnosis not supported by the large non-septate irregular hyphae.
Vomiting after months on a raw diet might suggest foodborne illness, yet direct visualization of hyphae in persistent gastric nodules establishes a specific invasive mycosis instead.
Mild mesenteric lymph-node enlargement is reactive in a case with fungal hyphae on gastric cytology and no neoplastic lymphoid population.
